Updated for launch: buggy mission quests with unclear direction that locks you out of permanent progress. Apparently this has been going on for months and is unaddressed still. Pros -Beautiful atmosphere -Great core concept of fighting off sea creatures and then mining materials for upgrades Cons -Glacially slow starting pace, almost laughable that miners would delve into the ocean bottom with such poor preparation: the combat bot is slow to move, slow to turn, slow to fire. The diver can barely carry resources. -Because of that glacially slow start, meta progression is taking a while to get going. -In the end, it's not fun, especially compared to peers in the adjacent genres What would make me recommend this game: Make the start more snappy in terms of mech speed/aiming and diver speed/carrying, compensate for difficulty with more enemies or more minerals required for upgrades.

这是一款类幸存者玩法的平面肉鸽游戏。 游戏是3D建模，但是建模水平不是非常精细，基本上就是独立游戏的标准水平，敌人种类到了后面也是重复的，总体来说水平一般。 优化稍微有点问题，到了后面敌人多了会有略微卡顿的现象，不过并不是特别影响体验。 没啥剧情，开局就是在海底，然后告诉你挖矿收集资源然后升级机甲打怪。 玩法其实就是穹顶守护者加类幸存者玩法。 玩家需要在地图上找矿洞，然后进去挖矿获得资源用来升级机甲和遗物，这部分玩法和穹顶守护者类似，不过每个矿洞都不是很大，里面的资源也是随机的。 然后每过一段时间（1分钟左右），地图上就会出现虫子，接着玩家只需要把来袭的虫子干掉就会又有一段时间用来寻找新的矿洞挖矿，直到玩家扛不住这局就算结束了。 一共有四种资源，三种是局内升级用的，可以用来升级武器威力，机甲速度，挖矿效率之类的，而另一种是局外资源，只要挖矿就能获得，用来解锁局外加成，比如新的机甲武器和技能，挖矿速度之类的。 虽然局外解锁项目加起来有十几个，但是总体来说内容还是比较少的，玩法到了后面也会比较单调，毕竟获得新的武器也只是加强一下攻击和速度之类的，没啥超武的说法。 另外游戏不支持鼠标，主炮塔没法用鼠标控制射击方向，不过手柄用着也还行。 有中文，不过翻译质量比较凑合。 总结 小品级的类幸存者游戏，喜欢这类游戏的话可以试试。 [quote]游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见[/quote]

[h1]机甲转呀转的射击，俺手持钻头挖呀挖的努力！[/h1] 《Codename: Ocean Keeper》是由RetroStyle Games自研自发的一款融合了机甲、挖矿、射击元素的幸存者类游戏，游戏里玩家需要操纵机甲进入水底探索，在地底裂缝处手持钻头离开机甲向下钻探挖取各种矿石，让自己在水底生存得更久一点！ 游戏的画面相当不错，虽说达不到精美的程度，但也能将海底元素一一呈现，各种充当怪物的海底生物也栩栩如生，机甲的战斗场景和各种武器效果更是相当炸裂，操作起来手感相当不错。 游戏玩法分为机甲射击求生时间和个人勘探时间，在时间倒数时需要将主角放入海底裂缝处进行钻探，获取矿石了再拉上机甲放好，获取矿石后随时可用来升级手上的钻头强度、钻头挖矿速度、和背后的动力机，至于升级顺序什么的，就全凭玩家自己喜欢了。 在时间倒数结束后，需要立马回去机甲操纵机甲开始战斗，如果时间内不回去，机甲会因为在外面被各种海洋生物攻击爆炸，导致游戏结束。同样的机甲也有着各种需要升级的属性，什么移动速度、血量上限、机甲上的各种武器的属性也一样都需要挖取来的各种矿石来升级，否则面对越来越强的海洋怪兽，基本坚持不到几波，更别说偶尔出现的BOSS大海怪了！ 每次战斗失败游戏会进入结算环节，之后可以用挖矿过程获得的货币在主页面升级机甲和个人科技，升级的类目与游戏过程用矿石升级的差不多，不过多了配备武器和技能的环节，在这里升级比游戏里升级重要多了，毕竟这也决定了每回游戏的初始。 整体而已，《Codename: Ocean Keeper》是一款相当优秀的游戏，无论是画面还是玩法，特别是新颖的机甲战斗个人挖矿设计，更是让游戏平白多出几分紧凑和刺激，不过目前RetroStyle Games是自研自发，宣发方面似乎并不够给力，知道这款游戏的玩家似乎并不多，只能说，再不宣传一下的话，就只能成沧海遗珠级的好游戏了！ [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402982/]走心评测[/url] ←遵从内心，写出真实感受 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ZXPC]走心评测[/url]←点击加入，一起探索游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]

Congratulations! Your team has done an exceptional job in being such terrible, awful, and lazy developers that I'm willing to take time out of my day to write a review! May 2nd: I buy the game at launch and it enjoy for 4 hours without issues. May 22nd: I see a "1.0.0 - Now Available and Optimized for Steam Deck" update and make the fatal mistake of playing this game on my steam deck. As part of the loadout tutorial, you need to purchase a mining bomb and equip it. Because I previously played on PC, I already had the mining bomb from my cloud save but the game thought I was a new player and forced me into tutorial again. Worse yet, this bugged state somehow transffered over the the Steam Cloud save so the game is unplayable on all devices. I see that a few complaining about this issue and decide to comeback later. June 3rd: New major patch touting a few new features and cross-platform. I download the game but the bug is still there preventing me from playing at all October 31st: A new "major" patch drops. I download the game and finally, the bug is fixed and I can finally play! Unfortunately, my save from previously is somehow bugged and I cannot access any new upgrades or quests so I have to make a new save but hey, its better than nothing. After a few hours, I get bugged again with no way to proceed. As part of the main questline, you need to complete ""puzzles"" to unlock important data to bring back to base and I use the puzzles extremely generously. Perhaps in your experience, a puzzle constitutes as simple matching—like seeing a red number and dialing the same number or connecting matching colored wires to terminals—but I think including puzzles that any four-year-old could solve wouldn't make for good gameplay. When dragging any of the aforementioned wires, if dropped near any wall, there's a chance that the wire will get stuck in the wall. Worse yet, somehow the state of the wire is saved so even after restarting the game, the wire will still be stuck in the wall. Grievances: -At least two gamebreaking bugs which have gone unfixed over half a year despite complaints -Mining is extremely tedious with no variations -Obvious mobile port with some downloading screens left in the game -Extremely unoptimized. I don't see why my RX 7900 needs to run a mobile game at medium to get more than 60 fps -Roguelite upgrades are uninspired with non-unlocks being +10% upgrades I typically don't offer criticism because on the off chance that it's taken to heart, the object of my criticism might improve themselves in some way. I'd prefer nothing more than for lazy, low-intelligence individuals like the developers to just keep making mobile games and never aspire to anyone with real responsibility. I wouldn't trust these devs to wash my car. TLDR: Game gamebreaking bugs for the past half year, uninspired gameplay, and is a poorly done mobile port. Do not buy.

Although the game is set at the bottom of the ocean, you could say it lacks depth. You'll grind for a lot of the permanent upgrades, and the story is simple without being rewarding unlike Wall World 2. The game draws natural comparisons to Wall World because you bounce from mine to mine trying to collect currency for permanent upgrades and mineable assets for temporary ones. The 3D mining rig defense is a bit more complex and adds some complexity, as do the graphics, but they don't really redeem it in comparison. The 8-bit simplicity is part of Wall World's charm. Hopefully the studio keeps making games and makes them more engaging. This one almost feels more like a demo. It's worth a buy on sale for a few hours of fun and an easily-obtainable 100% if you're OK with grinding.

I really like miner type games, and Ocean Keeper definitely tries to put a fresh spin on the genre. The mech aspect is genuinely cool and adds something different to the core loop that part works. Where it falls apart for me is depth. The story is extremely barebones, the upgrade system feels shallow, and a lot of the mechanics start to feel repetitive pretty fast. Some upgrades straight up don’t make sense either once your drill is fully upgraded, there’s basically no reason to ever use the fist or laser. The music was honestly the worst part for me. I hated it. It actively made the experience worse. After you finish the game, there’s almost zero motivation to replay it. No meaningful progression, no variation, nothing pulling you back in. I picked it up on sale and for that price, it was fine. But if I had paid full price, I would’ve been disappointed. It’ll keep you entertained for a day or two, then you’re done. 5/10

A mix of a digging game like Dome Keeper and a mech combat game, with technical issues and some not so well though-out mechanics. Good graphics and sound. Player/Mech movement is solid, though the environment is full of navigational obstacles. Pretty slow paced at first and you'll need some meta-progression to get started. There's plenty of weapons and utilities to try out and upgrade during each run. Some are good, others are a waste of time. You can't really make any builds though. Offered weapon slot upgrades are random and there's no reroll mechanism. Missions are weird. You can complete one, but there's no way to get back to a base or advance the story without dying. You literally have to fail a run to proceed to the next objective. Besides that, audio in the digging part got really muffled at some point. Not sure why but it didn't return to normal. And the game stopped responding to the controller once. On another try, the upgrade UI bugged out, showing overlapping controls. Fun for a while, but also very buggy and not much replayability. Development seems to be discontinued.
